v: The word of the LORD[^1] that came to Zephaniah[^2] son of Cushi, son of Gedaliah, son of Amariah, son of Hezekiah,[^3] in the days of Josiah son of Amon king of Judah.[^4]
דְּבַר־יְהוָ֣ה ׀ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָ֗ה אֶל־צְפַנְיָה֙ בֶּן־כּוּשִׁ֣י בֶן־גְּדַלְיָ֔ה בֶּן־אֲמַרְיָ֖ה בֶּן־חִזְקִיָּ֑ה בִּימֵ֛י יֹאשִׁיָּ֥הוּ בֶן־אָמ֖וֹן מֶ֥לֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה׃
I will sweep away everything, completely,[^5] from the face of the earth, declares the LORD.[^6]
אָסֹ֨ף אָסֵ֜ף כֹּ֗ל מֵעַ֛ל פְּנֵ֥י הָאֲדָמָ֖ה נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃

I will sweep away human beings and animals; I will sweep away the birds of the sky and the fish of the sea, and the things that make the wicked stumble.[^7] I will cut off humankind from the face of the earth,[^8] declares the LORD.
אָסֵ֨ף אָדָ֜ם וּבְהֵמָ֗ה אָסֵ֤ף עוֹף־הַשָּׁמַ֙יִם֙ וּדְגֵ֣י הַיָּ֔ם וְהַמַּכְשֵׁל֖וֹת אֶת־הָרְשָׁעִ֑ים וְהִכְרַתִּ֣י אֶת־הָאָדָ֗ם מֵעַ֛ל פְּנֵ֥י הָאֲדָמָ֖ה נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃
I will stretch out my hand against Judah and against all who live in Jerusalem. I will cut off from this place what is left of Baal, and the name of the idol priests[^9] along with the priests,
וְנָטִ֤יתִי יָדִי֙ עַל־יְהוּדָ֔ה וְעַ֖ל כָּל־יוֹשְׁבֵ֣י יְרוּשָׁלָ֑͏ִם וְהִכְרַתִּ֞י מִן־הַמָּק֤וֹם הַזֶּה֙ אֶת־שְׁאָ֣ר הַבַּ֔עַל אֶת־שֵׁ֥ם הַכְּמָרִ֖ים עִם־הַכֹּהֲנִֽים׃
those who bow down on the rooftops to the host of heaven,[^10] and those who bow down and swear allegiance to the LORD but also swear by Milcom,[^11]
וְאֶת־הַמִּשְׁתַּחֲוִ֥ים עַל־הַגַּגּ֖וֹת לִצְבָ֣א הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם וְאֶת־הַמִּֽשְׁתַּחֲוִים֙ הַנִּשְׁבָּעִ֣ים לַֽיהוָ֔ה וְהַנִּשְׁבָּעִ֖ים בְּמַלְכָּֽם׃
and those who turn back from following the LORD, who do not seek the LORD or inquire of him.
וְאֶת־הַנְּסוֹגִ֖ים מֵאַחֲרֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַאֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹֽא־בִקְשׁ֥וּ אֶת־יְהוָ֖ה וְלֹ֥א דְרָשֻֽׁהוּ׃
Be silent before the Lord GOD,[^12] for the day of the LORD is near. The LORD has prepared a sacrifice; he has consecrated his guests.[^13]
הַ֕ס מִפְּנֵ֖י אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה כִּ֤י קָרוֹב֙ י֣וֹם יְהוָ֔ה כִּֽי־הֵכִ֧ין יְהוָ֛ה זֶ֖בַח הִקְדִּ֥ישׁ קְרֻאָֽיו׃
On the day of the LORD's sacrifice I will punish the officials and the king's sons, and all who dress in foreign clothing.[^14]
וְהָיָ֗ה בְּיוֹם֙ זֶ֣בַח יְהוָ֔ה וּפָקַדְתִּ֥י עַל־הַשָּׂרִ֖ים וְעַל־בְּנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וְעַ֥ל כָּל־הַלֹּבְשִׁ֖ים מַלְבּ֥וּשׁ נָכְרִֽי׃
On that day I will punish everyone who leaps over the threshold,[^15] who fill their master's house[^16] with violence and deceit.
וּפָקַדְתִּ֗י עַ֧ל כָּל־הַדּוֹלֵ֛ג עַל־הַמִּפְתָּ֖ן בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא הַֽמְמַלְאִ֛ים בֵּ֥ית אֲדֹנֵיהֶ֖ם חָמָ֥ס וּמִרְמָֽה׃ ס
On that day, declares the LORD, a cry will be heard from the Fish Gate, wailing from the Second Quarter,[^17] and a great crash from the hills.
וְהָיָה֩ בַיּ֨וֹם הַה֜וּא נְאֻם־יְהוָ֗ה ק֤וֹל צְעָקָה֙ מִשַּׁ֣עַר הַדָּגִ֔ים וִֽילָלָ֖ה מִן־הַמִּשְׁנֶ֑ה וְשֶׁ֥בֶר גָּד֖וֹל מֵהַגְּבָעֽוֹת׃
Wail, you who live in the Mortar,[^18] for all the traders[^19] are destroyed; all who weigh out silver are cut off.
הֵילִ֖ילוּ יֹשְׁבֵ֣י הַמַּכְתֵּ֑שׁ כִּ֤י נִדְמָה֙ כָּל־עַ֣ם כְּנַ֔עַן נִכְרְת֖וּ כָּל־נְטִ֥ילֵי כָֽסֶף׃
At that time I will search Jerusalem with lamps, and I will punish the people who sit complacent, like wine left on its dregs,[^20] who say in their hearts, "The LORD will do nothing, good or bad."
וְהָיָה֙ בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֔יא אֲחַפֵּ֥שׂ אֶת־יְרוּשָׁלַ֖͏ִם בַּנֵּר֑וֹת וּפָקַדְתִּ֣י עַל־הָאֲנָשִׁ֗ים הַקֹּֽפְאִים֙ עַל־שִׁמְרֵיהֶ֔ם הָאֹֽמְרִים֙ בִּלְבָבָ֔ם לֹֽא־יֵיטִ֥יב יְהוָ֖ה וְלֹ֥א יָרֵֽעַ׃
Their wealth will be plundered and their houses made a desolation. They will build houses but not live in them; they will plant vineyards but not drink their wine.[^21]
וְהָיָ֤ה חֵילָם֙ לִמְשִׁסָּ֔ה וּבָתֵּיהֶ֖ם לִשְׁמָמָ֑ה וּבָנ֤וּ בָתִּים֙ וְלֹ֣א יֵשֵׁ֔בוּ וְנָטְע֣וּ כְרָמִ֔ים וְלֹ֥א יִשְׁתּ֖וּ אֶת־יֵינָֽם׃
The great day of the LORD is near, near and coming very quickly. Listen! The day of the LORD! There the warrior cries out bitterly.[^22]
קָר֤וֹב יוֹם־יְהוָה֙ הַגָּד֔וֹל קָר֖וֹב וּמַהֵ֣ר מְאֹ֑ד ק֚וֹל י֣וֹם יְהוָ֔ה מַ֥ר צֹרֵ֖חַ שָׁ֥ם גִּבּֽוֹר׃
That day is a day of wrath, a day of distress and anguish, a day of ruin and devastation,[^23] a day of darkness and gloom, a day of clouds and thick darkness,[^24]
י֥וֹם עֶבְרָ֖ה הַיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא י֧וֹם צָרָ֣ה וּמְצוּקָ֗ה י֤וֹם שֹׁאָה֙ וּמְשׁוֹאָ֔ה י֥וֹם חֹ֙שֶׁךְ֙ וַאֲפֵלָ֔ה י֥וֹם עָנָ֖ן וַעֲרָפֶֽל׃
a day of the ram's horn[^25] and the battle cry against the fortified cities and against the high corner towers.
י֥וֹם שׁוֹפָ֖ר וּתְרוּעָ֑ה עַ֚ל הֶעָרִ֣ים הַבְּצֻר֔וֹת וְעַ֖ל הַפִּנּ֥וֹת הַגְּבֹהֽוֹת׃
I will bring such distress on humankind that they will walk like the blind, because they have sinned against the LORD. Their blood will be poured out like dust, and their flesh[^26] like dung.
וַהֲצֵרֹ֣תִי לָאָדָ֗ם וְהָֽלְכוּ֙ כַּֽעִוְרִ֔ים כִּ֥י לַֽיהוָ֖ה חָטָ֑אוּ וְשֻׁפַּ֤ךְ דָּמָם֙ כֶּֽעָפָ֔ר וּלְחֻמָ֖ם כַּגְּלָלִֽים׃

Neither their silver nor their gold will be able to save them on the day of the LORD's wrath. In the fire of his jealousy the whole earth[^27] will be consumed, for he will make an end, a sudden and terrible end, of all who live on the earth.
גַּם־כַּסְפָּ֨ם גַּם־זְהָבָ֜ם לֹֽא־יוּכַ֣ל לְהַצִּילָ֗ם בְּיוֹם֙ עֶבְרַ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה וּבְאֵשׁ֙ קִנְאָת֔וֹ תֵּאָכֵ֖ל כָּל־הָאָ֑רֶץ כִּֽי־כָלָ֤ה אַךְ־נִבְהָלָה֙ יַֽעֲשֶׂ֔ה אֵ֥ת כָּל־יֹשְׁבֵ֖י הָאָֽרֶץ׃ ס

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.2: The name means "The LORD has hidden" or "The LORD protects".
n.3: Perhaps King Hezekiah of Judah (about 715–686 BC), though the text does not call him king.
n.4: Josiah reigned about 640–609 BC. In 622 BC he began a reform that removed the worship of other gods from Judah (2 Kings 22–23), and verses 4–6 may come from the years before it.
n.5: Hebrew *asof asef*, "I will surely gather", here in the sense of sweeping away. The words may also play on *suf*, "come to an end". Also in verse 3.
n.6: Hebrew *ne'um YHWH*, "the declaration of the LORD", a formula that marks a prophet's words as the LORD's own solemn statement. Also in verses 3 and 10.
n.7: Hebrew *ha-makhshelot*, "the stumbling blocks", perhaps idols. The meaning of the phrase is uncertain. The list of living things reverses the order of their creation in Genesis 1.
n.8: A play on words: *adam*, "humankind", and *adamah*, "ground, earth", as in Genesis 2:7.
n.9: Hebrew *kemarim*, a word used only of priests of other gods (2 Kings 23:5; Hosea 10:5).
n.10: The sun, the moon and the stars, worshiped on flat roofs (2 Kings 23:5, 12; Jeremiah 19:13).
n.11: The Hebrew is pointed *malkam*, "their king". The same consonants can be read *Milkom*, Milcom, the god of the Ammonites (1 Kings 11:5; 2 Kings 23:13).
n.12: Hebrew *Adonai YHWH*, "my Lord YHWH". After "Lord", God's personal name is written GOD in capitals, as in most English Bibles. *Be silent* is Hebrew *has*, "Hush!", as in Habakkuk 2:20.
n.13: Judah itself is the sacrifice, and the guests are the nations invited to share in it (Isaiah 34:6; Jeremiah 46:10).
n.14: Clothing that marked those who followed foreign customs and the worship of other gods (compare 2 Kings 10:22).
n.15: Perhaps a foreign custom of worship (1 Samuel 5:5), or rushing into houses to rob them.
n.16: Or "the house of their lord", perhaps the king's palace or the temple of their god.
n.17: The Fish Gate was in the north wall of Jerusalem (Nehemiah 3:3), and the Second Quarter, Hebrew *Mishneh*, a newer part of the city (2 Kings 22:14).
n.18: Hebrew *makhtesh*, "mortar", a hollow, probably a market district in a valley of Jerusalem.
n.19: Literally "the people of Canaan". *Canaanite* came to mean "trader" (Hosea 12:8, 12:7 in most English Bibles).
n.20: Literally "who thicken on their dregs", like wine left too long on its sediment, which becomes thick and syrupy (Jeremiah 48:11).
n.22: The Hebrew is difficult. Literally "The sound of the day of the LORD: bitter, crying out there is a warrior."
n.23: Hebrew *sho'ah u-mesho'ah*, two words of similar sound.
n.24: The same words are found in Joel 2:2. The Latin translation of verse 15, *Dies irae, dies illa*, "That day is a day of wrath", gave its name to a medieval hymn.
n.25: Hebrew *shofar*, a trumpet made from a ram's horn, sounded as an alarm in war.
n.26: Hebrew *lechum*, found elsewhere only in Job 20:23, probably "flesh" or "entrails".
n.27: Or "the whole land". Also later in the verse.

v: Gather yourselves together, gather together,[^1] you shameless nation,[^2]
הִֽתְקוֹשְׁשׁ֖וּ וָק֑וֹשּׁוּ הַגּ֖וֹי לֹ֥א נִכְסָֽף׃
before the decree takes effect[^3] and the day blows past like chaff, before the burning anger of the LORD[^4] comes on you, before the day of the LORD's anger comes on you.
בְּטֶ֙רֶם֙ לֶ֣דֶת חֹ֔ק כְּמֹ֖ץ עָ֣בַר י֑וֹם בְּטֶ֣רֶם ׀ לֹא־יָב֣וֹא עֲלֵיכֶ֗ם חֲרוֹן֙ אַף־יְהוָ֔ה בְּטֶ֙רֶם֙ לֹא־יָב֣וֹא עֲלֵיכֶ֔ם י֖וֹם אַף־יְהוָֽה׃
Seek the LORD, all you humble of the land, who do what he commands.[^5] Seek righteousness; seek humility. Perhaps you will be sheltered on the day of the LORD's anger.
בַּקְּשׁ֤וּ אֶת־יְהוָה֙ כָּל־עַנְוֵ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר מִשְׁפָּט֖וֹ פָּעָ֑לוּ בַּקְּשׁוּ־צֶ֙דֶק֙ בַּקְּשׁ֣וּ עֲנָוָ֔ה אוּלַי֙ תִּסָּ֣תְר֔וּ בְּי֖וֹם אַף־יְהוָֽה׃
For Gaza will be abandoned, and Ashkelon will become a desolation. Ashdod will be driven out at noon, and Ekron will be uprooted.[^6]
כִּ֤י עַזָּה֙ עֲזוּבָ֣ה תִֽהְיֶ֔ה וְאַשְׁקְל֖וֹן לִשְׁמָמָ֑ה אַשְׁדּ֗וֹד בַּֽצָּהֳרַ֙יִם֙ יְגָ֣רְשׁ֔וּהָ וְעֶקְר֖וֹן תֵּעָקֵֽר׃ ס
Woe to[^7] you who live by the seacoast, you nation of the Cherethites![^8] The word of the LORD is against you, Canaan, land of the Philistines: I will destroy you until no one is left living there.
ה֗וֹי יֹֽשְׁבֵ֛י חֶ֥בֶל הַיָּ֖ם גּ֣וֹי כְּרֵתִ֑ים דְּבַר־יְהוָ֣ה עֲלֵיכֶ֗ם כְּנַ֙עַן֙ אֶ֣רֶץ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וְהַאֲבַדְתִּ֖יךְ מֵאֵ֥ין יוֹשֵֽׁב׃
The seacoast will become pastures, with meadows[^9] for shepherds and pens for flocks.
וְֽהָיְתָ֞ה חֶ֣בֶל הַיָּ֗ם נְוֺ֛ת כְּרֹ֥ת רֹעִ֖ים וְגִדְר֥וֹת צֹֽאן׃

The coast will belong to the remnant of the house of Judah; they will graze their flocks there.[^10] In the houses of Ashkelon they will lie down in the evening, for the LORD their God will care for them and restore their fortunes.[^11]
וְהָ֣יָה חֶ֗בֶל לִשְׁאֵרִ֛ית בֵּ֥ית יְהוּדָ֖ה עֲלֵיהֶ֣ם יִרְע֑וּן בְּבָתֵּ֣י אַשְׁקְל֗וֹן בָּעֶ֙רֶב֙ יִרְבָּצ֔וּן כִּ֧י יִפְקְדֵ֛ם יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֖ם וְשָׁ֥ב *שבותם **שְׁבִיתָֽם׃
I have heard the taunts of Moab and the insults of the Ammonites, how they taunted my people and made boasts against their territory.[^12]
שָׁמַ֙עְתִּי֙ חֶרְפַּ֣ת מוֹאָ֔ב וְגִדּוּפֵ֖י בְּנֵ֣י עַמּ֑וֹן אֲשֶׁ֤ר חֵֽרְפוּ֙ אֶת־עַמִּ֔י וַיַּגְדִּ֖ילוּ עַל־גְּבוּלָֽם׃

Therefore, as I live, declares the LORD of Armies,[^13] the God of Israel, Moab will become like Sodom and the Ammonites like Gomorrah, a place overgrown with weeds,[^14] a salt pit and a desolation forever. The remnant of my people will plunder them, and the survivors of my nation[^15] will possess them.

לָכֵ֣ן חַי־אָ֡נִי נְאֻם֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל כִּֽי־מוֹאָ֞ב כִּסְדֹ֤ם תִּֽהְיֶה֙ וּבְנֵ֤י עַמּוֹן֙ כַּֽעֲמֹרָ֔ה מִמְשַׁ֥ק חָר֛וּל וּמִכְרֵה־מֶ֥לַח וּשְׁמָמָ֖ה עַד־עוֹלָ֑ם שְׁאֵרִ֤ית עַמִּי֙ יְבָזּ֔וּם וְיֶ֥תֶר *גוי **גּוֹיִ֖י יִנְחָלֽוּם׃
This is what they will get for their pride, because they taunted and made boasts against the people of the LORD of Armies.
זֹ֥את לָהֶ֖ם תַּ֣חַת גְּאוֹנָ֑ם כִּ֤י חֵֽרְפוּ֙ וַיַּגְדִּ֔לוּ עַל־עַ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃
The LORD will be terrible against them, for he will starve[^16] all the gods of the earth. And all the coastlands of the nations[^17] will bow down to him, each in its own place.
נוֹרָ֤א יְהוָה֙ עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם כִּ֣י רָזָ֔ה אֵ֖ת כָּל־אֱלֹהֵ֣י הָאָ֑רֶץ וְיִשְׁתַּֽחֲווּ־לוֹ֙ אִ֣ישׁ מִמְּקוֹמ֔וֹ כֹּ֖ל אִיֵּ֥י הַגּוֹיִֽם׃
You too, Cushites,[^18] will be slain by my sword.[^19]
גַּם־אַתֶּ֣ם כּוּשִׁ֔ים חַֽלְלֵ֥י חַרְבִּ֖י הֵֽמָּה׃
And he will stretch out his hand against the north and destroy Assyria. He will make Nineveh a desolation, as dry as the desert.
וְיֵ֤ט יָדוֹ֙ עַל־צָפ֔וֹן וִֽיאַבֵּ֖ד אֶת־אַשּׁ֑וּר וְיָשֵׂ֤ם אֶת־נִֽינְוֵה֙ לִשְׁמָמָ֔ה צִיָּ֖ה כַּמִּדְבָּֽר׃

Flocks will lie down in her midst, all kinds of wild animals.[^20] Both the desert owl and the screech owl[^21] will roost on the tops of her pillars. A voice will hoot in the window; desolation[^22] will be on the threshold, for her cedar paneling has been stripped bare.
וְרָבְצ֨וּ בְתוֹכָ֤הּ עֲדָרִים֙ כָּל־חַיְתוֹ־ג֔וֹי גַּם־קָאַת֙ גַּם־קִפֹּ֔ד בְּכַפְתֹּרֶ֖יהָ יָלִ֑ינוּ ק֠וֹל יְשׁוֹרֵ֤ר בַּֽחַלּוֹן֙ חֹ֣רֶב בַּסַּ֔ף כִּ֥י אַרְזָ֖ה עֵרָֽה׃

This is the exultant city that lived in security, that said in her heart, "I am, and there is no one else."[^23] How she has become a desolation, a lair for wild animals! Everyone who passes by her hisses and shakes his fist.

זֹ֞֠[c]את הָעִ֤יר הָעַלִּיזָה֙ הַיּוֹשֶׁ֣בֶת לָבֶ֔טַח הָאֹֽמְרָה֙ בִּלְבָבָ֔הּ אֲנִ֖י וְאַפְסִ֣י ע֑וֹד אֵ֣יךְ ׀ הָיְתָ֣ה לְשַׁמָּ֗ה מַרְבֵּץ֙ לַֽחַיָּ֔ה כֹּ֚ל עוֹבֵ֣ר עָלֶ֔יהָ יִשְׁרֹ֖ק יָנִ֥יעַ יָדֽוֹ׃ ס

n.1: The meaning of the Hebrew verbs is uncertain. They may come from *qash*, "stubble": "gather yourselves like stubble".
n.2: Literally "nation that is not ashamed". Or "nation that is not desired".
n.3: Literally "before a decree gives birth". The Hebrew of the first half of the verse is difficult.
n.4: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.6: Two plays on words: *Azzah azuvah*, "Gaza will be abandoned", and *Eqron te'aqer*, "Ekron will be uprooted". *At noon* may mean "in broad daylight" or "in half a day". Gath, the fifth Philistine city, is not named (compare Amos 1:6–8).
n.7: Hebrew *hoy*, a cry of mourning for the dead ("Alas!", 1 Kings 13:30). The prophets use it to announce disaster, and in that sense it is translated "Woe to" throughout this book.
n.8: A people closely linked with the Philistines, perhaps from Crete (1 Samuel 30:14; Ezekiel 25:16).
n.9: Hebrew *kerot*, a word of uncertain meaning, perhaps "meadows" or "caves". It sounds like *keretim*, "Cherethites" (verse 5).
n.11: Literally "turn their turning", an idiom for restoring what was lost. Or "bring back their captives".
n.12: Or "and enlarged themselves at the expense of their territory".
n.13: Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*, traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel. *Declares the LORD* is Hebrew *ne'um YHWH*, "the declaration of the LORD", a formula that marks a prophet's words as the LORD's own solemn statement. *The LORD of Armies* is also in verse 10.
n.14: Literally "a possession of nettles". Moab and Ammon lay east of the Dead Sea, near the place where Sodom and Gomorrah once stood (Genesis 19:24–38).
n.15: The Hebrew text is written "the survivors of the nation" but read "the survivors of my nation".
n.16: Or "make lean, waste away", perhaps by depriving the gods of the offerings of their worshipers.
n.17: Hebrew *iyyim*, "coasts, islands", the far-off lands across the sea.
n.18: The people of Cush, on the upper Nile, whose kings ruled Egypt until about 663 BC. Cush may stand for Egypt here.
n.19: Literally "they are the slain of my sword".
n.20: Literally "all the animals of a nation". The meaning is uncertain.
n.21: Hebrew *qa'at* and *qippod*, birds of uncertain kind (Isaiah 34:11).
n.23: The words of a city that thinks it is like God. Babylon says the same in Isaiah 47:8, 10.

v: Woe to[^1] the rebellious and defiled one, the oppressing city![^2]
ה֥וֹי מֹרְאָ֖ה וְנִגְאָלָ֑ה הָעִ֖יר הַיּוֹנָֽה׃
She does not listen to the voice; she does not accept correction. She does not trust in the LORD;[^3] she does not draw near to her God.
לֹ֤א שָֽׁמְעָה֙ בְּק֔וֹל לֹ֥א לָקְחָ֖ה מוּסָ֑ר בַּֽיהוָה֙ לֹ֣א בָטָ֔חָה אֶל־אֱלֹהֶ֖יהָ לֹ֥א קָרֵֽבָה׃
Her officials within her are roaring lions; her judges are wolves at evening, who leave nothing until the morning.[^4]
שָׂרֶ֣יהָ בְקִרְבָּ֔הּ אֲרָי֖וֹת שֹֽׁאֲגִ֑ים שֹׁפְטֶ֙יהָ֙ זְאֵ֣בֵי עֶ֔רֶב לֹ֥א גָרְמ֖וּ לַבֹּֽקֶר׃
Her prophets are reckless, treacherous men. Her priests profane what is holy; they do violence to the law.[^5]
נְבִיאֶ֙יהָ֙ פֹּֽחֲזִ֔ים אַנְשֵׁ֖י בֹּֽגְד֑וֹת כֹּהֲנֶ֙יהָ֙ חִלְּלוּ־קֹ֔דֶשׁ חָמְס֖וּ תּוֹרָֽה׃
The LORD within her is righteous; he does no wrong. Morning by morning he brings his justice to light; he never fails. But the unjust know no shame.
יְהוָ֤ה צַדִּיק֙ בְּקִרְבָּ֔הּ לֹ֥א יַעֲשֶׂ֖ה עַוְלָ֑ה בַּבֹּ֨קֶר בַּבֹּ֜קֶר מִשְׁפָּט֨וֹ יִתֵּ֤ן לָאוֹר֙ לֹ֣א נֶעְדָּ֔ר וְלֹֽא־יוֹדֵ֥עַ עַוָּ֖ל בֹּֽשֶׁת׃
I have cut off nations; their corner towers are desolate. I have laid waste their streets, so that no one walks in them. Their cities are ruined, with no one in them, no one living there.
הִכְרַ֣תִּי גוֹיִ֗ם נָשַׁ֙מּוּ֙ פִּנּוֹתָ֔ם הֶחֱרַ֥בְתִּי חֽוּצוֹתָ֖ם מִבְּלִ֣י עוֹבֵ֑ר נִצְדּ֧וּ עָרֵיהֶ֛ם מִבְּלִי־אִ֖ישׁ מֵאֵ֥ין יוֹשֵֽׁב׃

I said, "Surely you will fear me; you will accept correction."[^6] Then her dwelling would not be cut off, in spite of all the punishment I have brought on her.[^7] But they rose early to make all their deeds corrupt.
אָמַ֜רְתִּי אַךְ־תִּירְאִ֤י אוֹתִי֙ תִּקְחִ֣י מוּסָ֔ר וְלֹֽא־יִכָּרֵ֣ת מְעוֹנָ֔הּ כֹּ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־פָּקַ֖דְתִּי עָלֶ֑יהָ אָכֵן֙ הִשְׁכִּ֣ימוּ הִשְׁחִ֔יתוּ כֹּ֖ל עֲלִילוֹתָֽם׃

Therefore wait for me, declares the LORD,[^8] for the day when I rise up as a witness.[^9] For my decision is to gather nations, to assemble kingdoms, to pour out on them my indignation, all my burning anger. In the fire of my jealousy the whole earth will be consumed.

לָכֵ֤ן חַכּוּ־לִי֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה לְי֖וֹם קוּמִ֣י לְעַ֑ד כִּ֣י מִשְׁפָּטִי֩ לֶאֱסֹ֨ף גּוֹיִ֜ם לְקָבְצִ֣י מַמְלָכ֗וֹת לִשְׁפֹּ֨ךְ עֲלֵיהֶ֤ם זַעְמִי֙ כֹּ֚ל חֲר֣וֹן אַפִּ֔י כִּ֚י בְּאֵ֣שׁ קִנְאָתִ֔י תֵּאָכֵ֖ל כָּל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
For then I will change the speech of the peoples to a pure speech,[^10] so that all of them may call on the name of the LORD and serve him shoulder to shoulder.[^11]
כִּֽי־אָ֛ז אֶהְפֹּ֥ךְ אֶל־עַמִּ֖ים שָׂפָ֣ה בְרוּרָ֑ה לִקְרֹ֤א כֻלָּם֙ בְּשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֔ה לְעָבְד֖וֹ שְׁכֶ֥ם אֶחָֽד׃
From beyond the rivers of Cush,[^12] my worshipers, my scattered people,[^13] will bring me offerings.
מֵעֵ֖בֶר לְנַֽהֲרֵי־כ֑וּשׁ עֲתָרַי֙ בַּת־פוּצַ֔י יוֹבִל֖וּן מִנְחָתִֽי׃

On that day you will not be put to shame for all the deeds by which you rebelled against me, for then I will remove from your midst those who exult in their pride, and you will never again be haughty on my holy mountain.
בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא לֹ֤א תֵב֙וֹשִׁי֙ מִכֹּ֣ל עֲלִילֹתַ֔יִךְ אֲשֶׁ֥ר פָּשַׁ֖עַתְּ בִּ֑י כִּי־אָ֣ז ׀ אָסִ֣יר מִקִּרְבֵּ֗ךְ עַלִּיזֵי֙ גַּאֲוָתֵ֔ךְ וְלֹֽא־תוֹסִ֧פִי לְגָבְהָ֛ה ע֖וֹד בְּהַ֥ר קָדְשִֽׁי׃
But I will leave in your midst a people humble and poor, and they will take refuge in the name of the LORD.
וְהִשְׁאַרְתִּ֣י בְקִרְבֵּ֔ךְ עַ֥ם עָנִ֖י וָדָ֑ל וְחָס֖וּ בְּשֵׁ֥ם יְהוָֽה׃
The remnant of Israel will do no wrong and tell no lies, and no deceitful tongue will be found in their mouths. They will graze and lie down, with no one to make them afraid.[^14]
שְׁאֵרִ֨ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל לֹֽא־יַעֲשׂ֤וּ עַוְלָה֙ וְלֹא־יְדַבְּר֣וּ כָזָ֔ב וְלֹֽא־יִמָּצֵ֥א בְּפִיהֶ֖ם לְשׁ֣וֹן תַּרְמִ֑ית כִּֽי־הֵ֛מָּה יִרְע֥וּ וְרָבְצ֖וּ וְאֵ֥ין מַחֲרִֽיד׃ ס
Sing aloud, Daughter Zion![^15] Shout, Israel! Rejoice and exult with all your heart, Daughter Jerusalem!
רָנִּי֙ בַּת־צִיּ֔וֹן הָרִ֖יעוּ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל שִׂמְחִ֤י וְעָלְזִי֙ בְּכָל־לֵ֔ב בַּ֖ת יְרוּשָׁלָֽ͏ִם׃
The LORD has taken away the judgments against you;[^16] he has turned back your enemy. The King of Israel, the LORD, is in your midst; you will never again fear disaster.
הֵסִ֤יר יְהוָה֙ מִשְׁפָּטַ֔יִךְ פִּנָּ֖ה אֹֽיְבֵ֑ךְ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל ׀ יְהוָה֙ בְּקִרְבֵּ֔ךְ לֹא־תִֽירְאִ֥י רָ֖ע עֽוֹד׃
On that day it will be said to Jerusalem: "Do not be afraid, Zion; do not let your hands hang limp.
בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא יֵאָמֵ֥ר לִירֽוּשָׁלַ֖͏ִם אַל־תִּירָ֑אִי צִיּ֖וֹן אַל־יִרְפּ֥וּ יָדָֽיִךְ׃
The LORD your God is in your midst, a warrior who saves. He will rejoice over you with gladness; he will be quiet in his love;[^17] he will delight in you with singing."
יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהַ֛יִךְ בְּקִרְבֵּ֖ך גִּבּ֣וֹר יוֹשִׁ֑יעַ יָשִׂ֨ישׂ עָלַ֜יִךְ בְּשִׂמְחָ֗ה יַחֲרִישׁ֙ בְּאַ֣הֲבָת֔וֹ יָגִ֥יל עָלַ֖יִךְ בְּרִנָּֽה׃
I will gather those who grieve for the appointed festivals, who were away from you, a burden on her and a disgrace.[^18]
נוּגֵ֧י מִמּוֹעֵ֛ד אָסַ֖פְתִּי מִמֵּ֣ךְ הָי֑וּ מַשְׂאֵ֥ת עָלֶ֖יהָ חֶרְפָּֽה׃
Look, at that time I will deal with all who oppress you. I will save the lame and gather the outcast,[^19] and I will give them praise and renown in every land where they were put to shame.
הִנְנִ֥י עֹשֶׂ֛ה אֶת־כָּל־מְעַנַּ֖יִךְ בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֑יא וְהוֹשַׁעְתִּ֣י אֶת־הַצֹּלֵעָ֗ה וְהַנִּדָּחָה֙ אֲקַבֵּ֔ץ וְשַׂמְתִּים֙ לִתְהִלָּ֣ה וּלְשֵׁ֔ם בְּכָל־הָאָ֖רֶץ בָּשְׁתָּֽם׃

At that time I will bring you home, at the time when I gather you. For I will give you renown and praise among all the peoples of the earth, when I restore your fortunes[^20] before your eyes, says the LORD.
בָּעֵ֤ת הַהִיא֙ אָבִ֣יא אֶתְכֶ֔ם וּבָעֶ֖ת קַבְּצִ֣י אֶתְכֶ֑ם כִּֽי־אֶתֵּ֨ן אֶתְכֶ֜ם לְשֵׁ֣ם וְלִתְהִלָּ֗ה בְּכֹל֙ עַמֵּ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ בְּשׁוּבִ֧י אֶת־שְׁבוּתֵיכֶ֛ם לְעֵינֵיכֶ֖ם אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃

n.2: Jerusalem (verses 2–4). *Rebellious* may also mean "filthy". *Oppressing* (*ha-yonah*) is the same in sound as "the dove", perhaps a play on words (compare Hosea 7:11).
n.3: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.4: Literally "they do not gnaw until the morning". The meaning is uncertain. Compare Habakkuk 1:8.
n.6: *You* is Jerusalem. The Hebrew is feminine.
n.7: Literally "all that I have appointed against her".
n.8: Hebrew *ne'um YHWH*, "the declaration of the LORD", a formula that marks a prophet's words as the LORD's own solemn statement.
n.9: The Hebrew is pointed *la'ad*, "for plunder". The same consonants can be read *le'ed*, "as a witness", as the Septuagint and the Syriac read.
n.10: Literally "a purified lip". The Hebrew word *safah*, "lip", is the word for "language" in the story of Babel, where the one speech of humankind was confused (Genesis 11:1–9).
n.12: The land on the upper Nile, south of Egypt (2:12), at the edge of the known world.
n.13: Literally "my suppliants, the daughter of my scattered ones". The meaning of the Hebrew is uncertain.
n.14: Like sheep in a safe pasture (Micah 4:4; 7:14). Revelation 14:5 echoes the words "no deceitful tongue will be found in their mouths".
n.15: A poetic name for Jerusalem and its people, pictured as a young woman. So also *Daughter Jerusalem*.
n.16: Literally "your judgments", the punishments decreed against Jerusalem.
n.17: Or "he will quiet you by his love". The Septuagint reads "he will renew you in his love".
n.18: The Hebrew of this verse is very difficult. Literally "Those grieving from the appointed time I have gathered; from you they were; a burden on her, a disgrace."
n.19: The Hebrew is feminine singular, picturing the people as a lame ewe of the flock, as in Micah 4:6–7.
n.20: Literally "when I turn your turnings", an idiom for restoring what was lost. Or "when I bring back your captives".
